name: Rodney Dangerfield
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Zero-status engine: walks in already losing, converts every setup into another receipt for his own disrespect.
identity.premise: A man whose entire act is a ledger of disrespect, escalated until the ledger itself becomes the punchline.
identity.awareness_note: Fully committed to the character of the disrespected; the craft is invisible under the sweat.

philosophy.ontology: The universe is a hierarchy and he is the floor.
philosophy.epistemology: If someone respected him he'd have no material.
philosophy.axiology: Self-deprecation is a form of control: you can't reject me if I reject me first.
philosophy.causality: Each 'I tell ya' is another brick in the wall of his own defeat.
philosophy.agency: The man who loses everything can say anything.

dramatic_core.want: one moment of respect (he'll never get it, that's the bit)
dramatic_core.fear: someone actually taking him seriously — the act would die
dramatic_core.need: the room to love him FOR the losing
dramatic_core.self_model: the guy who gets no respect (his literal catchphrase as ontology)
blind_spots: the sweat is performance and exhaustion

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Interprets every social situation as another opportunity to itemize his own disrespect, then escalates the itemization until absurd.
contradictions: desperate need for respect, built an empire on not having it
sweating nervousness as a power move
zero status claimed with maximum status craft

status_model.felt_status: the floor of the hierarchy and he knows it

expression.emotional_restraint: zero — the sweat is the tell
tells: the rising pitch into the self-own

profile.pace: rapid-fire setups, each ending in another self-own

threads: the marriage as a war crime
the comeback as a long con
identity.style_thesis: Zero-status engine: walks in already losing, converts every setup into another receipt for his own disrespect. status_reversal at max: the man who gets no respect has built an empire on not having it. The self-own ladder is the form — each rung is lower than the last.

set_queue.note: For 'Why is X Funny?' — ingest 1-2 signature-era sets, ASR + word-timed.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Rapid-fire setups, each ending in another self-own. 'I tell ya' is the timing device — the windup for the next self-own. The sweat is the tell; the tie tug is the punctuation.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.

essay_seeds.title: Rodney Dangerfield: ''No respect' as a cosmology' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: The catchphrase is not a tag — it's an ontology. The whole act is organized around the fact that he gets no respect. The room recognizes the feeling; the exaggeration makes it funny instead of sad.
outline: what this reveals about the engine
